The projection of 0-crossing Voronoi vertices was proposed as a specific technique within this framework to ensure that the extracted mesh vertices lie accurately on the zero-level set of the inferred SDF, overcoming the limitations of naive interpolation methods [S1].

The claim states that the projection of 0-crossing Voronoi vertices was proposed as a specific technique to ensure mesh vertices lie on the zero-level set, overcoming limitations of naive interpolation. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes this method under the section 'Projection of 0-crossing Voronoi vertices'. It details how circumcenters (Voronoi vertices) can lie far from the tetrahedron, making barycentric interpolation (naive method) unreliable. It then presents the robust strategy: projecting the four sites of the tetrahedron to the zero-level set, fitting a plane to these projected sites, and projecting the Voronoi vertex onto this plane. The text confirms this ensures the vertex lies on the zero-level set using site-based information, avoiding the issues of naive interpolation.
